title: An Exposition of the Old and New Testament (Commentary on the Whole Bible), Volume II: Joshua to Esther
author: Matthew Henry
allowedUseNotes: Public-domain early-18th-century commentary (published 1708-1710 in six volumes, the OT historical books completed by Henry himself before his 1714 death, long pre-1928). May be cited, quoted in short excerpt, or paraphrased freely with attribution; no full-chapter reproduction needed per this project's own tighter internal policy regardless.
summary: Classic early-18th-century verse-by-verse devotional-critical commentary on the whole Bible by the English Nonconformist minister Matthew Henry, one of the most widely reprinted English commentaries of any period. On 2 Samuel 3:22-30 (Joab's killing of Abner), Henry reads Joab's stated motive (blood vengeance for Asahel, 3:27b, 30) as real but not the whole story: he reads Joab as also moved by professional jealousy at Abner's approach to David, on the reasoning that had Abner been received into David's service he might have been preferred above Joab as commander, and that Joab "could better bear the guilt of blood than the thoughts of a rival" — an explicit political/rank-rivalry motive alongside the blood-vengeance one the text itself states. This project cites Henry for that narrower point (a named, checkable historic reading of Joab's killing of Abner as partly power-motivated, not solely vengeance) as one of two scholarlyViews on claim-abner-killing (view-abner-killing-rival-elimination), presented alongside rather than replacing the text's own stated blood-vengeance motive (view-abner-killing-blood-vengeance).
